instruction:
Please act as a professional Verilog designer. Your task is to create a Verilog module that implements a frequency synthesizer block using either a phase-locked loop (PLL) or direct digital synthesis (DDS) method. 
A frequency synthesizer block is a digital circuit that generates a high-frequency output signal from a lower-frequency input signal. 
The output signal can be tuned to any frequency within a certain range, and it is often used in applications such as radio communication and signal processing.

Your module should have the following inputs and outputs:

Inputs: a reference clock signal (clk_ref), a control signal for selecting the synthesis method (ctrl), and a frequency tuning word (ftw). 
The reference clock signal is the input signal to the frequency synthesizer block, and its frequency is typically much lower than the output frequency. 
The control signal is used to select either the PLL-based or DDS-based synthesis method. 
The frequency tuning word is a digital word that determines the output frequency of the synthesizer block based on the selected synthesis method.

Outputs: a high-frequency output signal (out). 
The output signal should have a frequency that is a multiple of the reference clock frequency, and its frequency should be determined by the frequency tuning word and the selected synthesis method.

To implement the frequency synthesizer block, you should use Verilog code to define the PLL or DDS method as a function of the frequency tuning word and the reference clock signal.
You should then use this function to connect the inputs to the output signal. 
Finally, you should use the output signal to generate the high-frequency output signal based on the selected synthesis method.
